description: ATC — operational metrics covering HTTP, webhook ingestion, PG outbox+drain pipeline, watermarks, retention, startup/shutdown lifecycle, process resource usage, and operator-facing config reloads. Replica identity comes from the scraper as the `pod` label. Histogram panels query the classic `_bucket` series form; operators whose OTel collector is configured to emit only native histograms must translate to `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(name[5m])))` (no `_bucket`, no `le` group). See docs/architecture/metrics.md § Histogram aggregation.

panels.title: Replica build info
panels.description: atc_build_info gauge — one series per replica, value always 1.0. Use this to verify rollout state and see which version each pod is running.

panels.title: HTTP req/s
panels.description: Cluster-wide HTTP request rate aggregated across all routes.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx/s
panels.description: Cluster-wide HTTP 5xx error rate. Red above 0.01/s (one error every 100 seconds).

panels.title: HTTP p99
panels.description: Cluster-wide HTTP request duration p99 across all routes. Yellow >0.5 s, red >2 s.

panels.title: Runner pools loaded
panels.description: atc_config_runner_pools — number of operator-declared runner pools currently in AppState. Empty (0) is healthy when no runner-pool config is mounted; non-zero matches the loaded ConfigMap. Per-replica observation; max across pods is the cluster-wide value (within the kubelet sync window).

panels.title: Request rate by route + method
panels.description: Per-route + method request rate from axum-otel-metrics 0.13.0's http.server.request.duration histogram count series. `http.route` is the matched Axum route pattern (e.g. /v1/state, /v1/webhooks/github).

panels.title: Status code distribution
panels.description: Stacked status code rate. Use to spot a sudden surge of 4xx/5xx without losing the 2xx baseline.

panels.title: Latency by route — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Per-route p50/p95/p99 of http_server_request_duration_seconds. Histograms use the classic `_bucket` series (the OTLP→Prometheus translator emits classic histograms by default; see docs/architecture/metrics.md § Histogram aggregation for the native-histogram caveat).

panels.title: Error rate by route (5xx)
panels.description: Per-route 5xx rate. A non-zero rate on /v1/webhooks/github is the GitHub webhook ingestion path failing — see backend-server.md § webhook handler for the failure-mode triage.

panels.title: HTTP duration heatmap
panels.description: Cluster-wide HTTP duration distribution across all routes. Heatmap renders the native histogram bucket counts as a 2-D density plot — useful for spotting a multimodal latency distribution that p99 alone masks.

panels.title: atc_pg_notify_emitted_total by kind
panels.description: Successfully committed write transactions that emitted a pg_notify on `atc_outbox`. Split by event kind (run / job). Per-replica counter — sum across pods for cluster ingestion volume.

panels.title: atc_pg_write_failures_total by kind
panels.description: Webhook writes failing inside PgStore::apply_*_event. `kind=parity` = PG UPSERT matched 0 rows (page); `kind=transient` = sqlx error (alert on sustained rate). See metrics.md § atc_pg_write_failures_total.

panels.title: atc_pg_in_memory_drift_total
panels.description: Events where PG commit succeeded but the in-memory state machine apply diverged. Sustained non-zero rate is a state-machine bug — page. See metrics.md § atc_pg_in_memory_drift_total.

panels.title: NOTIFY received vs drain passes per pod
panels.description: atc_pg_notify_received_total (every NOTIFY each replica's listener saw) overlaid with atc_pg_drain_passes_total (NOTIFY-driven drain passes that actually fired). A NOTIFY-vs-pass divergence on a single pod means the drain task is wedged on that replica.

panels.title: Drain pass duration p99
panels.description: p99 of atc_pg_drain_pass_duration_seconds — wall time per NOTIFY-driven drain pass including paginated batches. Heartbeat-only ticks (5s readiness tick with no work) don't record observations.

panels.title: Outbox lag p99 (event age at broadcast)
panels.description: p99 of atc_pg_outbox_lag_seconds — `clock.now() - row.inserted_at` at broadcast. Includes writer-side transaction latency (PG `inserted_at` = transaction start). Yellow at 1 s, red at 5 s.

panels.title: Wake-coalesced rate
panels.description: Rate of atc_pg_wake_coalesced_total — NOTIFY arrivals observed while a drain pass was in flight. Sustained high values = NOTIFY storm relative to drain throughput.

panels.title: Drain throughput — rows/s and passes/s
panels.description: atc_pg_drain_rows_total (outbox rows fetched) and atc_pg_drain_passes_total. Disambiguates 'drain is slow' from 'drain has nothing to do'.

panels.title: Drain duplicate-skipped rate
panels.description: atc_pg_drain_duplicate_skipped_total — outbox rows fetched but suppressed by the ring-buffer dedup (re-fetched in a gap-healing rescan). Brief non-zero is normal reorder; sustained high rate means the drain is repeatedly rescanning the same range.

panels.title: Drain unknown-kind events (1h increase)
panels.description: atc_pg_drain_unknown_kind_total — outbox rows whose `kind` is neither `run` nor `job`. CHECK constraint should keep this flat zero in healthy deployments. Non-zero = deploy skew or schema invariant violation; page on first observation.

panels.title: Listener recv errors
panels.description: atc_pg_listener_recv_errors_total — errors that escaped sqlx's silent listener-reconnect loop. Non-zero rate over more than one scrape = listener can't recover (likely DSN session-mode misconfig).

panels.title: Watermark vs min_pending_seq (per pod)
panels.description: atc_pg_broadcast_watermark (solid) — highest seq this replica has broadcast — overlaid with atc_pg_min_pending_seq (dashed) — lowest pending NOTIFY seq below the watermark. Divergence (dashed < solid) = gap-healing rescan in flight. NaN renders as gaps (sentinel for caught-up state).

panels.title: Cluster floor — atc_pg_outbox_min_replica_watermark
panels.description: MIN(broadcast_watermark) across non-stale replicas — the safety floor the retention sweep uses to bound deletions. Refreshed every 30 s by the outbox heartbeat task. NaN = no live replicas heartbeated recently (cluster partition / shutdown).

panels.title: Oldest outbox row age
panels.description: atc_pg_outbox_oldest_row_age_seconds — age of MIN(inserted_at). Healthy steady state oscillates near outbox_retention. Monotonic climb past retention = sweep not deleting (check atc_pg_outbox_rows_deleted_total rate; verify heartbeats).

panels.title: Retention sweep rate — atc_pg_outbox_rows_deleted_total
panels.description: Cluster-wide outbox deletion rate. Each replica's sweeper handles a disjoint subset under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so sum across pods for the cluster total.

panels.title: Drain startup latency p99 (1h)
panels.description: atc_pg_drain_startup_seconds p99 — wall time from initial COALESCE(MAX(seq),0) watermark seed through first drain pass exit. One observation per process lifetime. Panel mostly empty between deploys.

panels.title: Drain shutdown remaining rows p99 (24h)
panels.description: atc_pg_drain_shutdown_remaining_rows p99 — outbox rows above this replica's watermark at drain task exit time. Sustained > DRAIN_BATCH_SIZE (500) prompts a drain-pass tuning review or longer terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

panels.title: Process CPU (percent of host)
panels.description: process_cpu_usage from opentelemetry-system-metrics 0.31.0 — value is `raw_cpu_percent / core_count`, normalized 0..100% of host capacity. Aggregated `max by (pod)` to collapse per-process attributes (pid, executable, command) into one series per pod.

panels.title: Process resident memory
panels.description: process_memory_usage — physical RSS in bytes. Aggregated `max by (pod)`.

panels.title: Process virtual memory
panels.description: process_memory_virtual — committed VSZ in bytes. Aggregated `max by (pod)`.

panels.title: Process disk I/O
panels.description: process_disk_io split by direction (read / write). Rate-of-change of total bytes read/written by the process.

panels.title: Config reload rate by result + reason
panels.description: atc_config_reload_total split by `result` (success/failure) and `reason` (applied/noop/read/parse/validate). A sustained `result=failure` rate means operator's most-recent YAML edit is invalid and the cluster is running on the previous good config. See metrics.md § atc_config_reload_total.

panels.title: Loaded runner-pool count over time
panels.description: atc_config_runner_pools — surfaces operator hot-reload events as step changes in the loaded pool count.

title: ATC — Overview
